source.title: Costly avoidance triggered by categorical fear generalization

confidence_rationale: Deliberately filed as 'unknown' direction: this paper does not bear on whether MECH-028 is true. It bears on whether one of the claim's two READOUTS is a valid construct. It establishes that over-generalised avoidance is separately measurable, imposes real cost, and dissociates from the fear response itself -- which is what makes 'avoidance cost' a usable dependent variable rather than a restatement of harm recurrence. Confidence reflects the quality of that methodological warrant, not support for the claim.
failure_signatures: Avoidance and fear generalisation gradients are dissociable -- participants avoided generalised stimuli at a cost, and reductions in costly avoidance tracked reductions in US expectancy rather than fear per se. A REE design that treats avoidance cost as a proxy for harm learning will therefore conflate two dissociable quantities.

Generalisation here is CATEGORICAL (conceptual category membership), not perceptual similarity. REE's avoidance-cost readout over non-harm resources presumes some generalisation gradient exists in the substrate; if V3's resources carry no category structure, the readout may have nothing to generalise along and will read null for a reason that has nothing to do with mode transitions.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Fear acquired to a conditioned stimulus generalised to novel stimuli belonging to the same conceptual category as the threat stimulus, but not to items from a fear-irrelevant category; participants then avoided those generalised stimuli even though avoidance carried an explicit cost. Reductions in costly avoidance aligned with reductions in unconditioned-stimulus expectancy, suggesting that behavioural approach can facilitate extinction.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-028's CONFIRMING criterion names two readouts: harm recurrence, and the avoidance COST -- approach-suppression of non-harm resources, i.e. over-generalised avoidance -- in the post-transition mode. This paper is the construct-validity warrant for the second readout: it shows that over-generalised avoidance is a real, separately measurable behaviour that people pay for, and that its magnitude is not simply read off the fear response. That is what makes the (B) arm's predicted 'hypervigilance lock' a distinguishable outcome rather than a redescription of the (C) arm's harm recurrence.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This paper says nothing about mode transitions, cognitive modes, or cross-state preservation, and should not be counted as evidence for or against MECH-028's substantive content. It is admitted here for readout validity only. The generalisation mechanism it uses is conceptual-category membership in humans, which V3's resource structure may not possess; if not, the avoidance-cost readout has no gradient to express itself along.
mapping.source_context: Healthy human adults; laboratory fear-acquisition training followed by a costly avoidance test with explicit response cost.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality good (well-regarded clinical-experimental venue, standard costly-avoidance paradigm). Mapping fidelity deliberately mid: the mapping is to the DEPENDENT VARIABLE, not to the claim, and the aggregate should not be read as support. Transfer risk covers the category-structure assumption V3 must satisfy for the readout to have any range.
